column2: but it also caused the market forces to react and it was suddenly alright to pay more for animals living in relative good circumstances.

column3: some of them in order to prevent infections and diseases

column1: Some examples of this are for instance the hormone stuffed broilers
column2: the antibiotic treated pigs and the crazy cows.

column1: Another reason is the modern society we live in

column1: At the beginning it was very expensive to live on vegetables and only the rich and educated could afford it.

The expensive- and exclusiveness disappeared when the average consumer claimed his right to this lifestyle and the market had to adjust itself to the demand and supply.

column2: it is a general awareness of our bodies and our health and many eating disorders are symptoms of this physical awareness.

column1: Lastly we have the environmental awareness.

column2: which combined with air and water becomes the acid rains that pollute our environment.

column1: Today 's generation is well aware of the environmental situation that they have inherited and by consuming less meat the production must eventually decrease.

column2: today it is profitable to sell less meat and more vegetarian alternatives.

column1: We want to feel good about ourselves and the market wants to make money.

\﻿ The number of cellular phones in Sweden still increases  Everywhere you go you see people talking in cellular phones.
In Sweden today
column2: the cellular phone has become even more common than the ordinary stationary telephone; in the autumn of 1999
column3: accordning to numbers then presented by the Swedish government
column4: nearly 5 million Swedes - about 55 per cent of the Swedish population - owned at least one cellular phone each.

column1: This means that the number of cellular phones has gone from practically zero to five million in only ten years.
And maybe even more extraordinary is the fact that the number just keeps increasing.
What could be the reason for this continuing boom?
Without doubt one reason is that many people want to be reachable as often as possible.
For instance they may have jobs where it's absolutely essential that they are reachable at any time of the day.
The cellular phone becomes an important part of their jobs and they wouldn't make it without it.

And I'm certain that one reason why so many teenage girls and boys are equipped with cellular phones is that parents want to be able to reach their children as soon as the slightest trace of worry emerges in their easily worried parental minds.
They don't mind paying for a phone
column2: but see it as some kind of insurance.

column1: Furthermore
column2: this habit of being reachable is addictive - once you've tried it
column3: it's hard to stop.

column1: Once you've bought your first cellular phone
column2: you may be hooked.

column1: On the other hand
column2: a great deal of people don't like to be reachable all the time
column3: and they are less likely to buy cellular phones.

column1: So the reachability part can't be the only reason for the huge number of cellphones sold in Sweden.
Another reason could be - fashion.
The cellular phone has become more than just a phone.
Today the little piece of electronic parts comes in various shapes and colors
column2: equipped with many other functions than those of an ordinary telephone.

column1: To many people being the owner of the newest
column2: ""hottest"" cellular phone is just as important as having reasonably fashionable clothes.

column1: When a model gets too old
column2: it's a must to replace it with a newer one.

column1: There's no doubt that the manufacturers of cellular phones have succeeded in their advertising and marketing - when a new model is about to be released onto the market
column2: the excitement of the public can almost be compared to that of people at some car fair when Volvo is about to present a new family car.

column1: But then again
column2: there of course is a great number of people who don't care about being in fashion.

column1: So why do these people also purchase cellular phones?
A rather important reason
column2: naturally
column3: is the price.

column1: Ten
column2: or even five years ago
column3: a cellular phone was much more expensive than it is today.

column1: At the beginning of the nineties the cellular phone was considered an article of luxury
column2: owned by very important and/or very rich people only.

column1: Today
column2: this is not the case at all and the prices continue to fall
column3: allowing more and more people to buy cellular phones of their own.

column1: However
column2: the phones may be cheaper
column3: but the bills can become rather unpleasant if you use the phone frequently.

column1: And suppose mopeds were as cheap as cellular phones - would that mean that everybody would buy a moped?
That doesn't sound very probable.
So even if the price is right
column2: there must be another
column3: more important reason for all this phone-buying.

column1: Since the beginning of time
column2: man has strived for communication with other people - not only for business but also for pleasure and leisure.

column1: The means have varied a lot - smoke signals were used by the indians
column2: cave paintings even earlier and the Morse code only recently surrendered to more modern means of communication
column3: just to mention a few.

column1: And communication is still the thing that keeps everything going in our society.
Consequently
column2: the most important reason for the still increasing number of cellular phones in Sweden is the people's will to communicate - especially since it's possible to do it at a reasonable cost and with an easy-to-use portable device.

column1: Quite simply - people want and need to talk to each other
column2: and if the preferred ""face-to-face"" mode isn't available
column3: there is always the possibility of using a cellular phone.

column1: About ten years ago many people thought that the cellular phone was just a fad.

column2: Ericsson
column3: Siemens and Motorola keep coming up with new functions in their portable units their prognosis probably will come true.

column1: Because people will keep communicating - be that by speech
column2: text or pictures.

column1: \﻿ ""The rise and the fall of the Swedish school system""  At the beginning of the twentieth century Sweden was a country where both teachers and students were highly respected.

column2: whether he or she was rich or poor
column3: the same opportunities to get a well paid job.

column2: since he or she would be the one to lead their children into a brighter future.

column1: Unfortunately this beautiful picture has changed.
Today
column2: when our century is approaching its end
column3: people no longer regard nine years of compulsory school as something important nor something to be proud of.

column1: These nine years are rather seen as a boring episode which leads either to an underpaid job or another dull three years at upper secondary school.

column2: many seven-year-olds still have great expectations before beginning first grade.

column1: Sadly enough they soon find out that school is far from what they expected it to be.

What a student
column2: in Sweden in 1999
column3: can expect is a classroom with too many pupils
column4: old schoolbooks
column5: an underpaid and overworked teacher and an attitude towards school as something boring and useless.

column1: But it is not only the attitude towards school that has changed
column2: but also the attitude towards teachers.

column1: Instead of mentors who brighten the future of their students
column2: teachers are rather seen as a nuisance who nag about homework.

column1: So
column2: what has gone wrong; why does nobody no longer seem to respect or enjoy school?

column1: In an open letter to one of Sweden's largest newspapers the Swedish Liberal Party
column2: Folkpartiet
column3: blames the governing parties.

column1: According to Folkpartiet one of the major reasons for this change of attitude is that politicians have tried to create a school were all children are at the same level.
They have tried to create a school where all students are given the exact same opportunities and where no student should feel that he or she is not as bright as his or her fellow students are.
Although this certainly sounds like a very beautiful idea it has
column2: however
column3: not quite worked out the way that the politicians had planned it.

column1: In their striving to create the perfect school
column2: they have failed miserably.

column1: What has happened is that students who work faster than their peers have not been given any extra material to work on and have therefore not been given the opportunity to develop.
Some schools have stopped giving out homework since it has been considered unequal and unfair.
This due to the fact that some students receive more help from their parents when doing their homework
column2: while others more or less have had to manage on their own.

column1: And perhaps worst of all; the students who need extra help have not been given it since there is a lack of financial resources and teachers.

column2: but a place were you either struggle to keep up with your peers or just sit and wait
column3: since you do not have anything else to do.

column1: So
column2: what the politicians really have accomplished to create is: a country in which twenty per cent of the sixteen-year-olds cannot read or write properly when they finish ninth grade; a country which has fewer school days and much less homework than any other European country; and a country where students and teachers seem to have lost respect for one another.

column1: These are only some of the reasons why people tend to smile when I tell them that I am a student at teacher's college.

column1: \﻿ Death Penalty - Legalized Murder  Death penalty is practised all over the world.
Half of the world is still using it as legal punishment.
It is mainly used in Asia and in Muslim countries but also in America.
There are many reasons why the death penalty should be abolished.
There are numerous arguments against the death penalty and it is difficult to point to any single fact or argument as the most important.
Below are a number of extremely valid reasons why the practice of capital punishment should be eradicated.
Capital punishment does not deter crime.
There are several scientific studies that has failed to demonstrate that executions deter people from committing crime.
People who commit crimes normally don't expect to get caught and therefore the threat of capital punishment hasn't got any deterrent effect.
If someone wants to commit a crime severe enough to result in a death sentence he/she would be most unlikely to regard any consequences of such an act.
Courts are unable to prevent accidental execution of innocent people.
On several occasions innocent prisoners have been executed.
There are countless cases where evidence has come up proving the executed person's innocence.
An execution is irrevocable and should absolutely not be carried through unless the evidences are hundred per cent positive.
Normally they never are.
It has occurred too many times that evidence or some witness has appeared after trial or in worse
column2: after the sentence has been carried out.

column1: Executions are sometimes torture.
Prisoners who have been executed in the electric chair (in the United States) sometimes didn't die immediately.
On some occasions the hair begun to burn or the eyes popped out of their heads.
It has happened several times that a prisoner's heartbeat has continued even after the power had been switched off Race plays a role in who gets the death sentence.
Death penalty discriminates.
If the victim is black or white often plays an important role of whom being charged with capital murder or receiving death penalty.
This means that those who murdered whites are more likely to be sentenced to death than those who murdered blacks.
It's also proven that black murderers killing a white person runs a higher risk of being executed than white killers murdering a black person.
Among the charged persons receiving a death sentence the majority are poor and they are usually members of an ethnic or religious minority.
Executions are very expensive.
It is actually more expensive to execute a prisoner than keep him/her imprisoned for life (which normally means 40 years).
In Texas for example they can keep three persons in prison for life at the same costs as one execution.
The alternatives are preferable.
By ending a convict's life the state also eliminates the possibility of getting some important answers.
What is it that transforms a man into a killer?
How has the convict been affected by his surroundings such as family
column2: neighbourhood
column3: work etc.

column1: Maybe the answers would be to uncomfortable.
Perhaps they would point at social injustice and racial discrimination?
Maybe a long-term psychological investigation in some cases would show that the perpetrator is also a victim.
Another argument for imprisonment instead of death is (maybe surprisingly) that it's an easy escape.
It's agonizing and maybe painful during a brief moment but then it's all over whereas imprisonment for life under poor conditions with no chance of ever getting out seems far worse.
Further
column2: during the time of imprisonment convicts can be taught up as unskilled workers
column3: giving them a chance to repay to society at least a small portion of the damage they've caused.

Why is this the case?
There are a number of causes of this trend and in this essay I will primarily deal with two of these.

One of the most important causes
column2: as I see it
column3: is the cutbacks that have been made in the public sector in the last ten years.

column1: The schools have been forced to save money
column2: this has lead to worse working-conditions for the teachers

column1: By not investing money that is well needed society signals that the schools are not being given priority.

This in turn leads to the individual teacher generally being under a lot of stress
column2: and if the teacher do not have time for everybody weak pupils do not get the help they need and consequently fail.

column1: This is a failure for the school and the teachers and a contributing factor to the low status.

column2: which has a negative impact on the status.

column1: The other major cause that has lowered the status of the teachingprofession is the low salary.

When the salary is a way to value a profession a low salary will inevitably lower the status.
I also believe that the low salary discourages young people from becoming teachers and a profession that has difficulty recruiting will undoubtedly suffer from low prestige.
As I wrote above the cutbacks and the low salary are the two major causes for the loss of status of the teachingprofession.
